deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 23% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 10.1% = 10-year Treasury 5.1% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew 18% last year; 17%/yr over 3 years — the market expects faster growth than the company has recently delivered.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: 30% (3 years ago 51%, falling) — each $100 invested in the business (debt + equity, net of cash) earns about $30 a year after tax; return on shareholders' equity 30% (3 years ago 35%).

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Signed but not yet delivered (remaining performance obligations): $683.0B, up 72% from a year ago — about 2.0× the last 12 months of sales; customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $69.6B, up 13% from a year ago.

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 17%/yr over 3 years and 14%/yr over 5 years; operating margin today 47% vs a 5-year range of 41–47% (median 45%): near the top of a fairly narrow range.

deeper.title: Cash returned to shareholders

note.headline: Microsoft shrugs off a reported global outage; still a hold on stretched cash-flow value

summary.thesis: The business keeps improving in sales and margins, but the price already assumes free cash flow will rebound strongly from 60.0B. The reported outage hurts reputation more than earnings for now.
summary.decision: Long-term: hold, and add only near the 486.0–491.22 support zone. Swing: wait for a pullback to 504.96–512.76.
summary.act_at: add at 486.0–491.22; swing entry only at 504.96–512.76

note.happening: Microsoft closed at 523.88, up 0.17%, after several outlets reported a global outage that began in Outlook email and spread into a wider cloud disruption. The price sits inside its current zone of 515.65–524.43, between the flat 20-day average of 529.39 and the 50-day average of 519.0. The next earnings report is due 2027-01-27.
note.business: Nothing in today's data changes the business numbers. Last quarter, revenue grew 18.8% from a year earlier, up from 18.3% two quarters ago. Operating margin, the share of sales left after running costs, rose to 47.1% from 46.27%. Analysts raised next-year EPS (earnings per share) by 2.2% over the last 30 days to 24.2. The weak spot is cash. Trailing free cash flow, the cash left after heavy spending on data centers, fell to 60.0B from 78.0B. The filings also say each dollar invested now earns 30¢ a year, down from 51¢ three years ago. The outage is a reported operational failure. Its main risk is to trust and to how willing enterprise customers are to rely on the cloud business (general knowledge). The data has no sign of lost demand, and the near-flat price move points to a hit to sentiment, not to the outlook. At risk: the payback on heavy spending, and any lasting damage to reputation if outages repeat. Not at risk: the balance sheet, with net cash of 29.0B and liquidity of 64.5B.

worth.text: Valuation methods disagree sharply. A discounted cash flow model (today's value of future cash) built on the 60.0B trailing free cash flow gives 184.7 to 296.75, with a base of 223.82. All of these are far below the price. To justify 523.88 on that model, free cash flow would need to start growing at 41.5% a year. The model caps starting growth at 30%, and even that cap gives only 346.74. Measured against its own price-to-sales history, the stock looks fair: 475.73 low, 535.43 middle, 592.92 high. The price sits below the middle. Against peers it is expensive, at 11.2 times sales versus a peer median of 4.1. It trades at 27.3 times trailing earnings and 21.6 times next-year earnings. The whole gap comes down to one question: is today's depressed cash flow the right base, or will earnings growth carry through to cash? I use the own-history range for fair value. It treats the cash dip as a temporary result of heavy spending.
worth.key_assumption: The spending that cut free cash flow from 78.0B to 60.0B turns back into cash, so earnings (next-year EPS estimate 24.2), not today's cash flow, are the right basis for value.
